title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives Election in Washington's 7th Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for Washington's 7th Congressional District features four candidates in the August 4 top-two primary, including incumbent Democrat Pramila Jayapal seeking a sixth term. The district encompasses most of Seattle, along with Shoreline, Vashon Island, Lake Forest Park, and parts of Burien and Normandy Park. Jayapal, a national progressive leader and former chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, faces primary challenges from fellow Democrat Gwen Kirkland, Republican Nirav Sheth, and David Blomstrom of the Fifth Republic Party. The district is considered safely Democratic and is rated Safe D by nonpartisan election forecasters.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date. Washington's 7th District is a safely Democratic seat, and polling is rarely conducted for non-competitive races.

candidates.name: Pramila Jayapal
candidates.summary: Pramila Jayapal is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Washington's 7th District, first elected in 2016. She is a prominent progressive voice in Congress, having previously chaired the Congressional Progressive Caucus, and serves on the House Judiciary, Budget, and Foreign Affairs Committees. Prior to Congress, she served in the Washington State Senate and founded OneAmerica, the state's largest immigrant advocacy organization.

candidates.name: Nirav Sheth
candidates.summary: Nirav Sheth is a Republican candidate challenging incumbent Pramila Jayapal in Washington's 7th Congressional District. A U.S. Marine Corps veteran and former police officer in Lakewood, Washington, Sheth is an entrepreneur and business owner in Pierce County. Born in India, he emigrated to the United States in 2008, studied computer and electrical engineering, and his campaign focuses on public safety, immigration reform, economic affordability, and education.

candidates.name: Gwen Kirkland
candidates.summary: Gwen Kirkland is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Pramila Jayapal from the left in Washington's 7th Congressional District primary. A Seattle resident, Kirkland filed to run in the 2026 top-two primary election against Jayapal, positioning herself as a Democratic alternative. Limited public information is available about her background, though she has been listed on official ballots and voter guides.

candidates.name: David W. Blomstrom
candidates.summary: David W. Blomstrom is a candidate representing the Fifth Republic Party in Washington's 7th Congressional District primary. A frequent candidate who has previously run for Washington governor and other offices, Blomstrom's campaigns have drawn attention for fringe political views. He resides in Seattle and has a history of running on unconventional platforms.

forecast.rationale: No public opinion polling exists for this race. The forecast relies entirely on structural factors: Washington's 7th District encompasses most of Seattle and nearby suburbs, making it one of the most Democratic districts in the nation (Cook PVI D+34). Incumbent Pramila Jayapal is a well-established six-term incumbent and former chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus. Her general-election opponents are a Republican challenger (Nirav Sheth) and a minor-party candidate (David Blomstrom of the Fifth Republic Party), plus a fellow Democrat (Gwen Kirkland) in the top-two primary. Nonpartisan forecasters rate the seat Safe D. The district has not been competitive in any recent cycle. Confidence is tempered to medium only due to the complete absence of polling data; in all other respects the Democratic advantage is overwhelming.
